comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral classification system (C43-C59). Both evaluations find the methodology innovative and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes clear methodology and statistical validation, while peer reviewers praise technical advances and detailed behavioral profiling.

Strong agreement on starvation and circadian findings (C60-C70). OpenEval notes marginal non-significance for overall frequency (p=0.061) but supports main L-type event findings. Peer reviewers accept these claims without criticism, with Reviewer 3 explicitly summarizing results.

Agreement on circadian feeding patterns (C67-C69). OpenEval finds strong support for LQ event increases during meal-times. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of broader starvation/circadian analysis without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on FLIC signal validation (C71-C73). Both evaluations support the technical validation matching 332 video-scored events to FLIC signals. OpenEval emphasizes duration as key distinguishing feature, peer reviewers praise precise identification of fly behavior.

Agreement on homeostatic feeding measures (C74-C78). OpenEval supports starvation validation and notes sex difference interpretation is speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers endorse these findings as part of broader hedonic/homeostatic distinction without specific concerns about speculation.

Strong agreement on hedonic feeding signature (C79-C85). Both evaluations support the dissociation between event duration (increased) and number (unchanged) in hedonic environments. OpenEval emphasizes this as key finding; peer reviewers call it 'innovative and very compelling.'

Perfect agreement on sweetness vs. caloric content (C86-C90). Both evaluations strongly support arabinose/sorbitol control experiments demonstrating sweetness drives hedonic feeding. OpenEval emphasizes experimental design; Reviewer 3 explicitly describes and endorses these controls.

Perfect agreement on homeostatic-hedonic interaction (C91-C101). Both evaluations support starvation potentiation of hedonic feeding. OpenEval notes modest effect size and marginal enhancement; peer reviewers accept findings as consistent with mammalian literature without raising concerns about effect magnitude.

Strong agreement on CaMPARI mushroom body findings (C102-C106). OpenEval supports both pan-neuronal and MB-specific validation with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers praise this as 'proof of principle' and helpful for understanding brain coding of feeding control.

Strong agreement on circuit requirements (C107-C110, C119). Both evaluations support lobe-specific and PAM requirements for hedonic feeding. OpenEval emphasizes dissociation from homeostatic feeding; Reviewer 3 explicitly describes experiments and calls circuit identification a strength of the paradigm.

Perfect agreement on starvation rescue of inhibition (C111-C112). Both evaluations support this circuit interaction finding. OpenEval notes inference about independent circuits is reasonable but requires future work; peer reviewers accept as part of overall compelling circuit analysis.

Perfect agreement on main conclusions (C114-C115). Both evaluations strongly endorse the central finding of independent yet overlapping homeostatic and hedonic feeding systems. Editor calls it 'compelling evidence,' reviewers call application 'innovative and very compelling.'

Agreement on abstract claims (C4-C6). OpenEval finds abstract faithfully represents experimental results. Peer reviewers implicitly endorse by praising the overall findings these claims summarize, particularly the hedonic feeding duration signature (C4).

OpenEval evaluated background/literature review claims (C1-C42) as appropriately supported by citations and accurately representing the field. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than background material.

OpenEval evaluated claim C113 about feeding behavior complexity as reasonable inference supported by study findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific motivational claim.

OpenEval rated speculative model claims (C116-C127) as UNCERTAIN, noting the proposed MB model integrates findings but lacks direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this speculative model.
